title: Preparation of the intact rodent organ of Corti for RNAscope and immunolabeling, confocal microscopy, and quantitative analysis
protocol: Anesthetize the animal according to institutional ethical approval requirements.
Decapitate the mouse after verifying sufficient depth of anesthesia.
Bisect the skull sagittally using surgical scissors.
Sagitally bisect the palate using surgical scissors.
Isolate the inner ear from the temporal bone carefully.
Remove the brain with surgical scissors or spatula to expose the inner ear embedded in each temporal bone.
Using surgical scissors, remove sections of temporal bone containing the inner ear and transfer to ice-cold PBS.
Reconstitute temporal bones into ice-cold 4% PFA for quick fixation.
Dissect temporal bones into 0.4% PFA at 20°C–22°C for RNAscope.
Work with PFA in a fume hood with adequate ventilation.
Dissect organs of Corti in the appropriate external solution for electrophysiology.
Perform dissection of organs of Corti in preferred RNA preservation solution for bulk RNA sequencing.
Use 5-cm plastic petri dishes for dissections.
Position one pair of forceps around the inner ear at the junction between the cochlea and semicircular canals to hold the temporal bone against the bottom of the dissecting dish.
Remove the inner ear from the temporal bone using blunt forceps.
Transfer the isolated inner ear to a new 5-cm dissecting dish containing fresh ice-cold PBS, ice-cold or room temperature 4% or 0.4% PFA, external solution, or RNA preservation solution.
Repeat steps for isolating and transferring the second inner ear to ensure both are in the same dissecting dish.
Position one pair of forceps around the inner ear at the junction between the cochlea and semicircular canals.
Gently hold the inner ear against the bottom of the dissecting dish to make the oval and round windows and cochlear turns visible.
Using a blade of the forceps, gently scrape and chip a small hole in the bone covering the apical turn of the cochlea.
Ensure the hole is large enough to expose the apical turn without damaging the underlying lateral wall or organ of Corti.
Repeat these steps for the other inner ear.
Transfer both inner ears to ice-cold 4% PFA.
Fix the inner ears for 30 min to 3 h depending on the primary antibodies to be used.
Use blunt forceps to carefully remove the bone covering the roof of the utricle.
Use fine forceps to gently open the membranous labyrinth covering the utricular macula.
Remove the overlying otoconia.
Isolate the vestibular epithelia after fixation.
Transfer the inner ears into a dissecting dish with fresh, ice-cold PBS.
Position one pair of forceps around the inner ear at the junction between the cochlea and semicircular canals to hold it firmly against the bottom of the dish.
Use another pair of forceps to remove the bone covering the organ of Corti, starting from a hole made in the apex.
Gradually expand the hole to expose all turns and the most basal hook of the organ of Corti.
Peel the lateral wall away from the organ of Corti using fine forceps.
Begin by pinching the lateral wall at the apical turns and gradually remove it from the organ of Corti using an unwinding motion.
Insert one blade of the fine forceps underneath the basal hook and gently push up to detach the basal turn.
Work slowly around the basal turn until it is loose.
Insert one blade of the fine forceps between the apical turn of the organ of Corti and the modiolus, and gently push up to detach it.
Continue detaching each turn of the organ of Corti from the modiolus in a slow manner.
If necessary, use a small dissecting knife or microscissors to cut central projections of spiral ganglion cells for release.
Isolate the vestibular sensory epithelia if desired.
Use a pair of fine forceps to hold the organ of Corti.
Pinch the tectorial membrane at the apical turn using a second pair of fine forceps.
Gradually remove the tectorial membrane from the organ of Corti using an unwinding motion.
Remove any excess bone left attached to the organ of Corti.
Transfer the organ(s) of Corti to a 24-well cell culture plate for RNAscope or immunostaining.
Fill each well of the 24-well plate with 300 to 400 μL of solution for RNAscope and immunostaining.
Place one to four organs of Corti into a single well as required by the specific experiment.
Exchange solutions using a micropipettor while samples remain in the same well.
Transfer samples gently between wells using fine forceps.
Turn on HybEZTM hybridization oven.
Prepare target probe in hybridization solution.
Aliquot C1 probes directly.
Pre-warm probe diluent to 40°C for 10 minutes.
Cool probe diluent to room temperature.
Centrifuge C2 or C3 probes briefly.
Dilute 2 μL of C2 or C3 probe in 100 μL of probe diluent.
Wash samples (organs of Corti) in PBT20 for three times, each for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Dehydrate samples through increasing MeOH/PBT20 gradients: 50%, 75%, and 100%.
Rehydrate samples through decreasing MeOH/PBT20 gradients: 75%, 50%, and 0%.
Wash samples in PBT20 in a 24-well plate 3 times for 5 min each at room temperature.
Draw a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier with a PAP-pen on slides.
Place approximately 3 drops (50–75 μL) of Proteinase III inside the hydrophobic circle on the slide.
Transfer samples from the 24-well plate to the Proteinase III solution and incubate for 8 min at room temperature.
Stop protein digestion by moving samples back to a 24-well plate containing PBT20.
Wash samples in PBT20 3 times for 5 min each at room temperature.
Line the bottom of humidity control tray of the hybridization oven with paper towels moistened with distilled water.
Make a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on slides using a PAP-pen.
Place the slides on the slide rack.
Position the slides on the rack in the humidity control tray.
Pipette approximately 50–75 μL of the target probe hybridization solution into the center of each hydrophobic circle.
Incubate samples in the hybridization oven at 40°C for 15–18 h.
Transfer samples from the hybridization oven to a 24-well plate with 0.2× SSC.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC three times, each for 15 minutes.
Aliquot preamplifier hybridization solution (Amp1), signal enhancement solution (Amp2), amplifier hybridization solution (Amp3), horseradish peroxidase (HRP) and HRP-blocker.
Equilibrate these solutions to room temperature before use.
Pipette 75 μL of 4% PFA into a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on a slide.
Transfer samples into the PFA and fix for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 3 times 5 min each at room temperature.
Incubate samples in preamplifier hybridization solution (Amp1) in a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on a slide for 35 min at 40°C in the hybridization oven.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 3 times 15 min each at room temperature.
Incubate samples in signal enhancement solution (Amp2) in a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on a slide for 20 min at 40°C in the hybridization oven.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 3 times 15 min each at room temperature.
Incubate samples in amplifier hybridization solution (Amp3) in a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on a slide for 35 min at 40°C in the hybridization oven.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 3 times 15 min each at room temperature.
Incubate tissue in horseradish peroxidase (HRP) in a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on a slide for 15 min at 40°C in the hybridization oven.
Dilute 1 μL TSA® Plus fluorescein in 1500 μL TSA buffer.
Mix approximately 75 μL diluted fluorescein per sample.
Store extra diluted fluorescein light shielded at 4°C for up to one month.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 2 times for 2 minutes each at room temperature.
Incubate tissue in TSA Plus® fluorescein for 30 minutes at 40°C in the hybridization oven.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 2 times for 2 minutes each at room temperature.
Stop horseradish peroxidase reaction by incubating samples in HRP blocker in a circle-shaped hydrophobic barrier on a slide for 15 minutes at 40°C in the hybridization oven.
Wash samples in 0.2× SSC in a 24-well plate 2 times for 2 minutes each at room temperature.
Wash samples in 1× PBS in a 24-well plate twice, each wash lasting 2 minutes at room temperature.
Proceed directly to immunofluorescent staining or mount samples immediately after washing.
Store washed samples in 1× PBS if not proceeding with staining immediately.
Block and permeabilize samples in the blocking buffer for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Pause the protocol once isolated organs of Corti are placed in blocking buffer.
Store isolated organs of Corti submerged in blocking buffer at 4°C for days to weeks.
Incubate organs of Corti in primary antibody solution diluted in blocking buffer at room temperature for at least 4 hours or up to 48 hours.
Rinse samples with PBT three times for 10 min each at room temperature.
Remove PBT solution and add the secondary antibody solution diluted in blocking buffer.
Incubate organs of Corti in the secondary antibody solution at least 4 h or up to 24 h at room temperature.
Rinse samples with PBT three times for 10 min each and once with PBS at room temperature.
Mount prepared organs of Corti on glass microscope slides.
Place a drop of Vectashield on a clean microscope slide for each organ of Corti to be mounted.
Use fine forceps to transfer the piece(s) of organ of Corti into the drop of mounting medium.
Transfer samples using a lifting motion with the forceps to minimize damage to the organs of Corti.
Under a dissecting microscope, use the forceps to gently position the pieces so that the basilar membrane faces the slide and the organ of Corti faces the coverslip.
Cut the organ of Corti into two or three pieces before mounting if turns overlap to prevent them from overlapping.
Position segments of the organ of Corti close to each other on the slide for convenient subsequent imaging.
Allow organs of Corti to cool to 4°C if they are at room temperature.
Mount the organ of Corti carefully on a microscope slide.
Overlay a glass coverslip and adhere it with nail polish.
Label slides appropriately.
In Photoshop, open images to montage.
Go to File → Script → Load files into stack and select the images to montage.
In the layers panel, select all layers to be montaged.
Go to Edit → Auto Align Layers → Reposition.
Flatten layers by going to Layer → Flatten Image.
Make the canvas size larger in the original image by going to Image → Canvas Size.
Open the image to be added in a new window.
Use the rectangular marquee tool to outline the region of interest containing the segment to be added.
Copy (Ctrl-C) the selected segment.
In the original image, paste (Ctrl-V) the copied segment.
If necessary, reposition the copied segment using the Move Tool.
Once all segments have been incorporated into a single file, flatten layers by going to Layer → Flatten Image.
If necessary, crop extra canvas using the crop tool.
Save in RGB format as [filename]_merged.tif.
Download ImageJ from NIH.
Add "Measure_Line.class" to the directory ImageJ\Plugins\Tools.
Open the montaged/combined image in RGB format using ImageJ.
Go to Plugins → Tools → Measure Line.
Select the “segmented” line tool from the main toolbar.
Mark the length of each segment of organ of Corti from base to apex.
Click "d" after marking each segment.
Annotate for the selected species by clicking "a".
Identify specific tonotopic regions by selecting the “hand” tool and clicking "p".
Drag the hand across the annotated tonotopic map to identify exact frequencies.
Click on the tonotopic annotation to annotate with the exact frequency at that location.
Save the image with the overlaid frequency map in RGB format as [filename]_mapped.tif.
Select the appropriate lasers, filters, detection windows and scanning configuration depending on the fluorophores used.
Identify the appropriate tonotopic region under high magnification using low magnification images with superimposed maps.
Set the laser intensity, gain, and offset so that the brightest parts of the image are just saturated.
Repeat this step for the other fluorophores.
Adjust to ensure no “cross talk” between channels if necessary.
Identify the relative top and bottom of the region of interest in the stack of images.
Collect the required number of image stacks at optimal resolution.
View projections through the entire stack after scanning to verify correct region scanned.
